survived.where: Table 2 caption, Figure 1 caption, Table S3, Abstract — "Paired-bootstrap intervals on every difference are in the released artifact"; "each with the paired interval excluding zero"
survived.claim: Not one numerical interval for a GRAIL-versus-comparator difference appears anywhere in the manuscript or the SI, yet every headline claim is defined by such an interval.
survived.why: The paper's whole discipline is "a claim that the system leads is made for a cell only where that cell's interval excludes zero" (Section 2.8). The abstract, Section 3.1, Figure 1 and Section 5 all assert lead/trail verdicts, and the reader is given only point estimates (Table 2), colours (Figure 1) and +/-/· glyphs (Table S3). Every printed interval in the two documents belongs to an internal ablation (P1, P2, P3, Section 3.2, Section 3.3, Section 3.4, P5, Table S4); the comparison that the title, abstract and conclusions rest on has none. A referee cannot check whether any verdict is correct, cannot see how wide the intervals are, and cannot tell whether "leads at k=30" means a margin of 0.038 with an interval of [+0.001,+0.075] or [+0.020,+0.056]. Deferring them to a released artifact is not the same as reporting them: the SI is where they belong.
survived.fix: Add a differences panel to Table 2 (GRAIL's reported arm minus each comparator at each budget, with the paired 95% interval) and replace or supplement Table S3's glyphs with the difference and interval in each of the 45 cells.
survived.evidence:
THE ABSENCE IS REAL (verified exhaustively). Grepping both documents for bracketed intervals returns 18 hits: manuscript lines 114, 134, 151, 288-290, 311-312, 325, 334, 385; SI lines 214, 253-254, 258-261. Every one belongs to an internal ablation or registered prediction (P1/P2/P3/P5, the stage ablation, the selection ablation, the Tanimoto baseline, the merged-graph filter variant, the group oracle). None is a GRAIL-versus-comparator difference. Not an extraction artifact: numbers.tex defines 252 `gap.*` macros (7 arms x 9 budgets x point/lo/hi/sep, all from a pinned artifact) and `grep -o "\numGap[A-Za-z]*" body.tex si.tex` returns nothing — not one is typeset.

BUT EVERY GROUND FOR "FATAL" FAILS AGAINST THE TEXT:

1. The declared discipline is not breached. Section 2.8: "A claim that the system leads is made for a cell only where that cell's interval excludes zero, and where an ordering is not established the table says so." That governs which claims are made, not which statistics are printed, and the paper obeys it. Section 3.1: "Neither side separates at k = 8 and 10, where MetaPredictor leads, nor at k = 15 and 20." Section 4.3 opens: "GRAIL does not lead at the tight budgets."

2. The verdicts are correct. Checked against the pinned macros: gap.bankMetatox.15 = [-0.0185, +0.0611] (sep = no), gap.bankMetatox.20 = [-0.0103, +0.0647] (sep = no), gap.bankMetatox.30 = [+0.0046, +0.0723] (sep = yes), gap.bankMetatox.50 = [+0.0455, +0.1084] (sep = yes), gap.bankSygma.1 = [-0.093, -0.0344] (sep = yes). These reproduce Section 3.1 exactly, including "Against MetaTox alone ... the exhaustive mode leads at all nine budgets, with the interval excluding zero at seven of them" — k = 15 and 20 are the two that do not separate.

3. "A referee cannot check whether any verdict is correct" is contradicted. Section 2.8 specifies the estimator in full (Eq. 6, "B = 10 000 resamples", "the empirical 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles"), and Section 7 releases "the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator, the evaluation harness." SI S13: MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions "are frozen per substrate and released with the code." Every interval is recomputable.

4. The margins the finding says are invisible are printed. Table 2 gives all five arms at all nine budgets to four decimals: k = 30 is 0.6391 - 0.6015 = +0.0376 against MetaTox, k = 50 is 0.7038 - 0.6271 = +0.0767, k = 1 is 0.1053 - 0.1534 = -0.0481. The finding's own hypothetical ("a margin of 0.038") is answerable from Table 2 — it is +0.0376.

5. The interval's decision is reported at 45 cells, not merely at the headline. Table S3 caption: "Every cell is read from the interval and never from the point estimate." Figure 1 caption: "Shading is read from the paired intervals and not by eye."

6. The remedy is typesetting, not analysis: the values already exist as pinned macros, so no claim changes and nothing is recomputed.

WHAT SHOULD STILL REACH THE AUTHORS: the k = 30 lead over MetaTox is [+0.0046, +0.0723], a marginal exclusion a reader should see rather than infer from the ~0.034 half-widths reported elsewhere on the same population. Print the 63 intervals as an SI table beside Table S3. That is a minor revision request, not a fatal defect.

survived.where: Abstract / Section 1 / Section 5 and Section 2.4 versus Table S5 — "replacing their product with a rank fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data, more than any architectural change we tested"
survived.claim: The paper's single headline design number is the fusion-versus-product difference measured on a pool that is not the deployed one; on the deployed configuration the paper's own SI gives 0.0519 for the same contrast, same population and same budget, and the two are never reconciled.
survived.why: Table S5 (validation draw, n=293, k=15, pool "built by the deployed configuration and capped by rule score before any arm sees it") gives fusion 0.4748 and their product 0.4229, a difference of 0.0519. The text reports +0.0733. Checking numbers.tex resolves it: h7.fusion = 0.4489 and h7.product = 0.3756, and h9.uncapped = 0.4489 — i.e. P1 was measured on the uncapped pool, before the 100-candidate cap that the deployed system applies (Section 2.5, "mean pool 669.9 to 98"). So the number quoted in the abstract, the introduction and the conclusions describes a configuration the paper does not deploy, and it is 41% larger than the deployed-configuration value derivable from the SI. This also changes the registered verdict: 0.0519 sits at the registered threshold of +0.05 rather than comfortably above it, and it changes "more than any architectural change we tested", whose only quantified competitor is the merged pair-graph variant at −0.0090 (S5.2). A referee handed two values for one contrast, with the larger one in the abstract and the smaller one in the SI, cannot accept either as written.
survived.fix: State which configuration P1 was measured on wherever +0.0733 appears, and report the deployed-configuration fusion-versus-product difference (0.0519 on the validation draw at k=15) with its paired interval alongside it; use the deployed number in the abstract and conclusions.
survived.evidence:
THE TWO VALUES — SAME POPULATION, SAME METRIC, SAME BUDGET

Main text §1 (closing paragraph): "replacing their product with a rank fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data, more than any architectural change we tested." Repeated in §5: "Replacing the product of the two scores with that fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data, more than any architectural change we tested."

§2.4: "This was registered as prediction P1 with a threshold of +0.05 and evaluated on the validation split, where it had not been selected: +0.0733, 95% CI [+0.0477, +0.102]."

Table 4 caption fixes the metric: "P8's figure is a speed-up factor and P9's a median in seconds; the rest are differences in micro recall@15." Row: "P1 | rank fusion instead of a product of scores | +0.05 | +0.0733 | validation | H7".

§2.1 fixes the population: "Of these, 294 produced a candidate pool, and the 293 held by both arms of a paired comparison carry 655 references. Every registered ranking and timing threshold is checked here." P1 is a registered ranking threshold, so its population is the n=293 validation draw.

Table S5 gives the same contrast on the same 293: "validation draw, n = 293 — fusion (deployed) ... 0.4748 [k=15] ... their product ... 0.4229 [k=15]". Difference 0.0519. Its caption fixes the pool: "The pool is built by the deployed configuration and capped by rule score before any arm sees it, so the pool, the matching rule and the budget are fixed and only the order varies."

0.0519 is not ad-hoc arithmetic by the referee. Main-text Eq. (6) defines the paired statistic as delta = sum(h^A - h^B) / sum|Y|, which is identically the micro-recall difference, so 0.4748 - 0.4229 is exactly the paper's own estimator evaluated on the deployed pool.

PROVENANCE, FROM paper2/numbers.tex

  \numHSevenFusion  = 0.4489   % h7.fusion
  \numHSevenProduct = 0.3756   % h7.product    -> 0.4489 - 0.3756 = 0.0733
  \numHNineUncapped = 0.4489   % h9.uncapped
  \numHNineCapped   = 0.4748   % h9.capped     -> 0.4748 - 0.4489 = 0.0259 ~ h9.diff 0.026

P1's fusion arm (0.4489) is identical to P2's *uncapped* arm, and P2's *capped* arm (0.4748) is identical to Table S5's deployed fusion cell. P1 was therefore measured before the 100-candidate cap that §2.5 declares as part of the deployed system ("mean pool 669.9 to 98"). Neither \numHSevenFusion nor \numHSevenProduct is ever printed anywhere in body.tex or si.tex, so the reader sees only the difference and cannot detect this.

THE SI AFFIRMATIVELY STATES THE OPPOSITE

S8: "Table S5 is the full budget sweep for the ranking ablation of the main text."
S9: "The comparison in the main text is run on the deployed pool, capped at 100, where the budget is narrower than the pool for every substrate."

That is not an omission but a positive claim about the disputed number which the pinned artifact contradicts.

THE PAPER KNOWS THIS FAILURE MODE AND DISCLOSES IT TWICE, ELSEWHERE

S7: "Table S4 recomputes that oracle under four partitions of one candidate pool, on the deployed configuration rather than on the uncapped pool the original measurement used."
S8: "Both ran on a 245-substrate subsample under the superseded product ordering, so their levels do not transfer to the configuration reported here."

The exact disclosure the headline number needs is written twice in neighbouring sections and never applied to P1.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 0.0519 (why not fatal)

- Sign and direction unchanged; fusion still beats the product on the deployed configuration.
- The comparative claim holds: the only quantified architectural competitor is the merged pair-graph filter at "paired difference -0.0090, 95% CI [-0.017, -0.001], n = 1,170" (S5.2).
- The registered verdict does not flip. Table 4's criterion is a point estimate against a threshold (cf. P3, "<= +0.05", measured +0.0092); 0.0519 > 0.05 still passes, by 0.0019 instead of 0.0233.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING AS WRITTEN

1. "Abstract" is a wrong locator: +0.0733 does not appear in the abstract. It appears in §1 (final paragraph), §2.4, Table 4 (P1 row) and §5.
2. "This also changes the registered verdict" is overstated — the verdict still passes; only its margin collapses, and the paper supplies no interval for the deployed-configuration contrast.
3. A related defect the finding does not name: "more than any architectural change we tested" sets a validation-draw n=293 figure against a test-split n=1,170 figure (S5.2), which is itself a population mix under the paper's own rule.

survived.where: §2.3 Rule bank and SI S4: "It is the deduplicated union of four curated collections together with templates mined from the molecule-disjoint training split alone."
survived.claim: The four curated template collections that supply roughly 1,725 of the 7,581 rules (7,581 minus the 5,856 mined) are never named, cited, counted or licensed anywhere in the manuscript or the SI.
survived.why: The rule bank is the chemistry of this paper, and a reader cannot judge, reproduce or redistribute it without knowing where a quarter of it came from. It also cannot be ruled out that one of the collections is a comparator's own rule set — SyGMa's, GLORY/GLORYx's, or BioTransformer's 994 templates, all of which the paper cites and two of which it runs — in which case Table 2 is partly GRAIL re-ranking a comparator's own chemistry and the k=30/50 lead is not a comparison of independent systems. The omission also sits badly beside §3.6's "the half of the bank with no expert provenance", which asserts that the other half has provenance while never giving it, and beside the SI's careful licence analysis of the four corpus sources, which does not extend to the four rule sources.
survived.fix: Name and cite the four collections, give the template count each contributes after deduplication and their licences, and state whether any comparator's published rule set is among them; if it is, report Table 2 additionally with those templates removed.
survived.evidence:
The omission is real and exhaustive. The phrase appears twice, verbatim, and is never expanded:

- Manuscript §2.3: "The bank holds 7,581 templates spanning 4,417 distinct reaction types... It is the deduplicated union of four curated collections together with templates mined from the molecule-disjoint training split alone."
- SI S4: the identical sentence, plus "of which 7,580 parse under RDKit 2022.09.5."

Checks run over `.review/manuscript.txt` and `.review/si.txt`: "curated" occurs 2x in the manuscript (§2.3 and §3.6) and 10x in the SI (S4 once, the S11 worked-example prose once, 8 as a table-cell value). "collections" occurs once in each. Neither reference list contains a template-collection citation — 28 entries in the manuscript, S1–S9 in the SI, all of them corpora, comparators, standardisation, splitting, fusion or methodology.

The count is derivable but never printed. SI S4: "Support across mined templates is heavily skewed: 4,274 of 5,856 rest on a single training pair." 7,581 − 5,856 = 1,725. `mined.rules` is a pinned macro (`\numMinedRules{5,856}` in numbers.tex); there is no curated counterpart, and no bank-composition table anywhere.

The licence asymmetry is exact. SI S1 does the analysis for the corpus, in detail: "Their licences do not combine. ChEMBL 34 is released under CC BY-SA 3.0... MetXBioDB 1.0 is distributed with BioTransformer, whose terms require explicit permission for commercial use or redistribution." Nothing equivalent exists for the bank — while §7 states the bank is released and pinned: "A split manifest pins by digest the triple files, the substrate sets, the evaluated test set, the rule bank and all third-party artifacts," at a public repository. So a quarter of a redistributed artifact has undeclared provenance and undeclared terms, under a discipline the paper applies rigorously one section earlier.

The SI contents list in the manuscript promises "the rule bank and its mining procedure"; S4 delivers the mining procedure and the parse count, and for the curated quarter delivers the six-word clause above.

Two things the referee did not use, both of which strengthen the report:

1. §3.6 is not merely vague, it is arithmetically at odds with the SI. "All four rules here are mined rather than curated, so the half of the bank with no expert provenance is the half carrying this molecule." Mined is 5,856 of 7,581 — 77%, not half. This is the manuscript's only quantitative characterisation of the curated/mined split, and the composition table the finding asks for is exactly what would reconcile it. (A dedup subtlety makes it worse, not better: 1,725 is a lower bound on the curated collections' size, since a curated template duplicating a mined one collapses to one entry and the text does not say which label survives.)

2. The word "four" is load-bearing twice for two different things — "assembled from four sources: ChEMBL, DrugBank, MetXBioDB and the GLORYx reference set" (§2.1, named, versioned, licensed) and "four curated collections" (§2.3, none of the above). A reader who conflates them will believe the bank has been licence-cleared when it has not.

On the contamination escalation, the paper addresses only the opposite direction. §2.1: "their expert rules may encode the same metabolism reported in these sources; BioTransformer is built on MetXBioDB... in a direction that flatters them, and we report it rather than control it." The bank→comparator direction — GRAIL's curated quarter containing SyGMa's, GLORY/GLORYx's, or BioTransformer's "994 templates" (SI S13) — is neither raised nor excluded.

survived.where: Abstract ("against every comparator with predictions on the same substrates"); SI S13 Comparators ("BioTransformer is pinned by digest ... its 994 templates loaded at freeze time"); SI S10 ("the 150 substrates shared with a further comparator")
survived.claim: BioTransformer was obtained, pinned by digest and run, yet appears in no results table, and the rule by which it was excluded from the comparison is never stated.
survived.why: The abstract asserts a comparison against every comparator with predictions on the same substrates, and SI S13 sets out the authors' own rule that "a comparator that could not be obtained is reported as unavailable with its reason, is not dropped silently." BioTransformer was obtained and is silently absent from Table 2, Figure 1 and Table S3. Because the comparison population is the intersection of substrates on which every included method predicts, the choice to drop one comparator is simultaneously a choice of population: SI S10 records a 150-substrate population "shared with a further comparator" against the 291 reported here. A referee cannot tell whether the budget-divided verdict survives on the 4-comparator, 150-substrate set, and the reader has been told, incorrectly, that no such choice was made.
survived.fix: State explicitly which comparators were run, which are reported, and the pre-declared rule for inclusion; add BioTransformer as a column of Table 2 and a row of Table S3 (on the intersection it defines, reported as a named population), or, if it is excluded, give the reason and show that the reported verdict is unchanged on the population that includes it. Correct the abstract's claim accordingly.
survived.evidence:
The factual core is confirmed in the documents.

1. BioTransformer is recorded as obtained and pinned, in the section reserved for comparators. SI S13 "Comparators", in full: "SyGMa 1.1.0 is taken from the installed module. BioTransformer is pinned by digest rather than by version string, because '3.0' names several builds: jar c70cad91, 115,415,197 bytes, upstream commit 6432cf88 of 2023-05-25, its 994 templates loaded at freeze time rather than taken from a constant. MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions are frozen per substrate and released with the code."

2. It is in no results arm. Table 2's column head is exactly "k | GRAIL exh. | GRAIL int. | MetaTox | SyGMa | MetaPred." (confirmed in the typeset source, paper2/table_sweep.tex line 6). Figure 1's legend carries the same five series. Table S3 reports only "GRAIL's better arm ... the strongest comparator". Four comparators are pinned in S13; three appear anywhere in the results.

3. No exclusion rule covers it. S13's closing rule is written for a different case: "a comparator that could not be obtained is reported as unavailable with its reason, is not dropped silently, and the list is not extended after the first run." That rule governs the four 2025–26 systems that "could not be run on our split as released". Nothing in either document states a rule for a comparator that *was* obtained and is not reported.

4. The abstract's quantifier is exposed to this: "reports its performance under five matching criteria and ten output budgets against every comparator with predictions on the same substrates."

5. S10 leaves the fourth comparator unnamed: the two populations are "the 150 substrates shared with a further comparator and the full 1,170". The reader must infer from S13's roster which comparator that is.

But two load-bearing clauses of the finding do not survive.

(a) "the reader has been told, incorrectly, that no such choice was made" — the opposite is stated, twice, prominently. Main-text Limitations: "The comparison population is the 291 substrates on which all methods predict, a quarter of the evaluated test split and not a random quarter of it." SI S10 opens: "The comparison set is a quarter of the evaluated test split and not a random quarter, since it is fixed by which substrates every method returns predictions for." An entire SI section is titled "The choice of evaluation population". The population choice is declared, and its non-randomness is declared with it.

(b) "A referee cannot tell whether the budget-divided verdict survives on the ... 150-substrate set" — S10 reports precisely that test on precisely that population: it "re-ran three methods, four metrics and five criteria on two populations ... and asked whether the ordering of methods changes with the population. Of 60 pairwise comparisons, 10 reverse in point estimate, no population-by-method interaction separates from zero, and none survives a Holm correction," with the power bound declared ("detects an interaction of 0.0661 at 80% power, so it excludes large population effects and not moderate ones") and the design's weakness conceded.

(c) "yet ... run" is an inference, not text. S13 says predictions were frozen for MetaTox and MetaPredictor and that SyGMa is taken from the installed module; for BioTransformer it records only a digest and a template count read at freeze time. Note also SI S1: "MetXBioDB 1.0 is distributed with BioTransformer" — one of the four corpus sources ships inside that same jar, so a digest pin has a second, non-comparator reason to exist.

survived.where: Conclusions and Introduction, vs Table S5 (SI §S8). Conclusions: "Replacing the product of the two scores with that fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data"; Table 4 row P1: "+0.0733 ... validation". Table S5, validation draw, k=15: fusion 0.4748, their product 0.4229.
survived.claim: The paper's single headline design claim has two different values for the same contrast on the same population, and the larger one is the one that appears in the Introduction, the Conclusions and Table 4.
survived.why: P1 is defined as fusion-minus-product in micro recall@15 on validation; Table S5 reports exactly that contrast on the validation draw and it is +0.0519, not +0.0733. The underlying macros confirm two distinct measurements (h7.fusion 0.4489 / h7.product 0.3756 against rank.val.fusion15 0.4748 / rank.val.product15 0.4229, with rank.val.vsproduct pinned at 0.0519). Either P1 was measured on a superseded pool or on a different validation population, and the paper says neither. §3.9 then puts the +0.0733 on a common scale with retraining noise as if it were a current-configuration effect, and §2.1 forbids exactly this by declaring that every figure names its population. survived.fix: State in §2.4, Table 4 and the Conclusions which pool and which validation population P1 was measured on; if it is the superseded pool, report the deployed-configuration value (+0.0519, with its interval) as the headline and keep +0.0733 only as the registered check with a sentence saying the configurations differ.
survived.evidence:
POPULATION IS THE SAME — the paper says so itself.

§2.1 ("Which population carries which number"): "The validation draw is a declared sample of 300 substrates at seed 0 from the validation split. Of these, 294 produced a candidate pool, and the 293 held by both arms of a paired comparison carry 655 references. Every registered ranking and timing threshold is checked here, since a threshold checked where its rule was chosen is not a check."

P1 is a registered ranking threshold, so "validation" in Table 4 is the validation draw, n = 293 — exactly the row of Table S5. The population defence is closed by the paper's own sentence.

THE CONTRAST IS THE SAME.

Table 4 caption: "P8's figure is a speed-up factor and P9's a median in seconds; the rest are differences in micro recall@15." Row P1: "rank fusion instead of a product of scores | +0.05 | +0.0733 | validation | H7".

Table S5 (SI §S8, "Stage ablations on the deployed configuration"), validation draw, n = 293, k = 15: fusion (deployed) 0.4748, their product 0.4229 → +0.0519. §S8 states Table S5 "is the full budget sweep for the ranking ablation of the main text."

THE CAUSE, from paper2/numbers.tex — the two macro families are not two roundings of one measurement, and one identity settles it:

  \numHSevenFusion{0.4489}      % h7.fusion
  \numHSevenProduct{0.3756}     % h7.product   → h7.diff 0.0733
  \numHNineUncapped{0.4489}     % h9.uncapped   ← identical to h7.fusion
  \numHNineCapped{0.4748}       % h9.capped     ← identical to rank.val.fusion15
  \numRankValFusionOneFive{0.4748} / \numRankValProductOneFive{0.4229}
  \numRankValVsproduct{0.0519}, lo 0.0246, hi 0.0812

h7's fusion arm IS the uncapped pool of P2/H9. P1 was measured before the pool cap, on the configuration P2 replaced (0.4489 + 0.0260 = 0.4748). The deployed-configuration value of the same contrast is +0.0519 [+0.0246, +0.0812].

THE PAPER KNOWS HOW TO FLAG THIS AND DOES NOT HERE.

§2.5: the deployed pool is "arg top 100" — "Registered as prediction P2 ... mean pool 669.9 to 98."
§3.8: "the product ordering with each group emitted as a block on the uncapped pool. That is not the deployed ranking, so the figure bounds a configuration that is not deployed."
§S7: "Table S4 recomputes that oracle under four partitions of one candidate pool, on the deployed configuration rather than on the uncapped pool the original measurement used."
§S8: an earlier pair of ablations "ran on a 245-substrate subsample under the superseded product ordering, so their levels do not transfer to the configuration reported here."

WHERE THE UNFLAGGED NUMBER APPEARS.
Introduction: "replacing their product with a rank fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data, more than any architectural change we tested."
§2.4: "registered as prediction P1 with a threshold of +0.05 and evaluated on the validation split, where it had not been selected: +0.0733, 95% CI [+0.0477, +0.102]."
Table 4, row P1.
Conclusions: "Replacing the product of the two scores with that fusion is worth +0.0733 of recall on held-out data, more than any architectural change we tested."
§3.9: "the rank fusion of P1 is an order of magnitude larger than retraining noise and the pool cap of P2 several times larger" — an uncapped-pool effect and capped-pool effects put on one scale in one sentence.

CORROBORATION (not part of the finding, but same paragraph). §2.4's "On the set where the variant was chosen among four it gives +0.109" is typed literally in body.tex ($+0.109$), not macro-generated, and does not match Table S5's comparison set (0.5353 − 0.4376 = +0.0977, the pinned \numRankCmpVsproduct). survived.where: §7 Data and software availability, and Supporting Information Available: "prepared for deposit at [ZENODO DOI, minted on publishing the deposit], held until the licence position is settled"; "Whether they may be redistributed, and under which licence, is [CORPUS LICENCE: whether the derived corpus and the candidate pools may be redistributed, given DrugBank's terms]"
survived.claim: The Data Availability Statement is submitted with unresolved editorial placeholders and an explicitly undetermined licence, and the deposit it points to is deliberately withheld, so at the point of review the article has no data availability statement in the sense ACS Research Data Policy Level 2 requires.
survived.why: Level 2 requires a definite statement naming where the supporting data are, under what conditions, with a persistent identifier; where access is restricted, the restriction and the access route must be stated as facts, not as an open question the authors intend to resolve later. Here the licence question is posed to the reader rather than answered ('Whether that may be redistributed ... is [CORPUS LICENCE: ...]'), three Zenodo DOIs are unminted, and SI S14 confirms the upload is blocked ('the tool refuses to run without one: a Zenodo record cannot be withdrawn once published'). A referee cannot verify availability of data whose availability the authors themselves do not yet know, and the SI free-of-charge statement compounds it by pointing the Supporting Information at the same unminted Zenodo DOI rather than at the publisher.
survived.fix: Settle the licence position before resubmission and state the outcome as a fact; mint the Zenodo DOI (a closed or restricted-access record with a stated request procedure is acceptable under Level 2 if redistribution is genuinely barred) and replace all three placeholders with the real DOI; point the Supporting Information Available paragraph at the publisher's SI, not at the data deposit.
survived.evidence:
WHAT SURVIVES (the markers are real and do render in bold brackets):

§7: "The train and validation candidate pools are prepared for deposit at [ZENODO DOI, minted on publishing the deposit], held until the licence position is settled."
§7 and SI S1: "Whether they may be redistributed, and under which licence, is [CORPUS LICENCE: whether the derived corpus and the candidate pools may be redistributed, given DrugBank's terms]"

WHAT REFUTES THE CLAIM AS FRAMED:

1. §7 opens with a definite statement the finding does not quote:
"The data and software underlying this article are publicly available. Source code, the split manifest, the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator, the evaluation harness, the provenance sweep and the preregistration with every hypothesis and its outcome are at github.com/doctawho42/GRAIL, and are available to reviewers at submission."
A named persistent location, an itemised list, and explicit reviewer access at submission. The unfilled clauses qualify one bulk deposit, not the statement.

2. The restriction IS stated as fact, with cause and extent — SI S1:
"Their licences do not combine. ChEMBL 34 is released under CC BY-SA 3.0, which requires a derivative to carry the same or a compatible ShareAlike licence and forbids adding restrictions. DrugBank 5.1.10 is released under CC BY-NC 4.0, which forbids commercial use. A single derived work drawing on both cannot satisfy each: adding the non-commercial clause is a restriction ShareAlike does not permit, and dropping it breaches DrugBank's terms."
And the deposit's contents are enumerated rather than asserted: "What the deposited pools actually contain bears on this and is stated rather than assumed... The deposit is therefore a list of corpus substrates, hashes of their annotations, and our own predictions."

3. The access route and its verification are stated as fact — §7:
"The repository pins the SHA-256 of both the raw file and the uploaded archive in paper2/zenodo_manifest.json, and scripts/zenodo_deposit.py --verify checks a download against it, so the deposit is verifiable against the version used here rather than merely available."

refuted.claim: Saturation is evidenced by re-running a deterministic procedure on its own input, which can only reproduce its own output, and the paper's own support distribution is evidence against saturation.
refuted.why_refuted:
The finding's fatal severity rests entirely on its closing causal claim: that the saturation sentence "together with the invariance argument, is what licenses the abstract's 'a property of the annotation corpus rather than of our implementation'". The text says otherwise, in three places, in an unambiguous "X, making it Y" construction where X is the invariance and only the invariance. The abstract, the Conclusions, and §3.11 — the section that establishes the ceiling — each derive the corpus-property claim from the type-definition sweep (Table 5) plus the 42,554-template census, and none of the three mentions mining, saturation, or the re-run. Cut the saturation sentence entirely and the abstract, §3.11, Table 5, Figure 4 and the Conclusions are unchanged. No headline result rests on the check, vacuous or not.

The finding's second prong — that the paper "reads exactly this signature the other way elsewhere", taking 294 of 312 singleton miss types as proof of a long tail — is contradicted by the sentence it paraphrases. §3.11 explicitly declines that inference: "The table does not support the claim that 0.8724 of the gap is singletons under our definition. It supports a different one..." The paper refuses to lean on the singleton share precisely so that the bound does not depend on how finely a type is cut. There is no asymmetric reading to catch.

The third prong — that the support distribution is evidence against saturation — mixes two populations the paper keeps apart, which is the discipline the referee is invoking. 4,274/5,856 is support over mined templates from the training split; 294/312 is over missing reaction types in the test references; they carry different provenance keys in numbers.tex. And the Good–Turing reading does not contradict the paper's claim in any case: a high singleton share bounds the mass that would appear under MORE PAIRS from the population, whereas the paper's claim is explicitly scoped to re-running on the SAME SPLIT. The paper's very next sentence states the Good–Turing conclusion itself — "Extending coverage requires new reaction corpora" — so paper and referee agree on the substance. The finding reads a claim about the miner's exhaustiveness on a fixed input as a claim about the corpus's exhaustiveness on the task, then refutes the second.

The check is also not strictly vacuous. SI S4 documents a sampled acceptance filter (200 products on average over a 50-substrate sample) atop a timeout-bounded ring-aware MCS; exact bank reproduction across runs of such a pipeline is a real stability result, which is how the SI presents it, without the word "saturated".

What survives is a one-word wording point, worth a line in the response and nothing more: in §2.3 the colon presents the re-run as evidence for "saturated", and the re-run supports stability rather than exhaustiveness. Recommend the authors either split the sentence ("Support is heavily skewed; the mining is stable: re-running the miner on the same split re-derives every template it derived before and none new") or, in §4.4, replace "and mining is saturated" with "and re-mining the same split yields nothing further". That is a minor editorial correction to a sentence that licenses no result in the paper — not a fatal defect, and on the evidence above not a defect that should reach the authors framed as one.

refuted.claim: No run configuration is reported for any comparator, so the output lengths that produce the paper's only lead claims are undocumented defaults, while GRAIL's own emission was deliberately sized to fill the widest column.
refuted.why_refuted:
The finding accuses the paper of smuggling in an unstated confound. The paper states that confound as its own conclusion — in Results, in the Discussion subsection titled "What the numbers do not support", in Limitations, and in a dedicated SI section (S9) that derives the rule and reports the per-arm run-out counts. A finding whose entire "why" is quoted verbatim from the manuscript's Limitations cannot be fatal; it is the authors' position, not a defect they concealed.

Beyond that, four of the finding's load-bearing premises are false against the text: the lead claims are not confined to k=30/50 (seven interval-backed leads against MetaTox, including three tight budgets where nobody has exhausted, plus an explicitly length-matched cell at k=15); the comparator columns are exactly reproducible, since the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator are released and digest-pinned in the split manifest; GRAIL is not the only untruncated arm — its own interactive arm runs out on 282 of 291 lists and is reported doing so; and the §2.5 pool-cap sentence is an anti-tautology guard that the finding reads as its opposite.

What survives is narrow and editorial: S13 pins SyGMa by version and BioTransformer by digest but records no run configuration for any arm — no SyGMa scenario/steps/cutoff, no MetaTox access date, no MetaPredictor decoding settings. For a manuscript whose title is "under a fully declared evaluation", that is a fair request, and worth three lines in S13. It cannot move a number, because the numbers come from frozen, digest-pinned prediction files rather than from a re-run; and the one claim a different SyGMa scenario could perturb is the wide-budget advantage, which the paper has already booked as "partly a statement about output length on all sides rather than about ranking." Minor, not fatal. As drafted the finding should not reach the authors; the S13 configuration request should, on its own.
